description: Held-out intent corpus in two layers: real external phrasings and an authored gap layer. Report the layers separately; do not add them into one accuracy.

external.note: Real user phrasings from the public corpus named in external_manifest.json, labelled by hand. The corpus carries no usable intent labels; every gold value here was written against app/agent/intents.yaml.

authored_gap.note: Phrasings written for the intents the external layer does not contain or contains too few of, plus gaps closed by a human through the intent gap queue. Reported separately: it is coverage evidence, not a real-world frequency estimate.

intent_notes.SELF_ANALYTICS: Absent from the external layer: the corpus is a product Q&A stream whose users ask about one order at a time, and it contains no aggregate question about the caller's own records. All evidence for this intent is authored.
intent_notes.HUMAN_HANDOFF: The external layer has 10 cases, but they say '店长/负责人/管事的/客服电话' rather than the catalog's '转人工' wording; that is why the intent is kept in the table with a real denominator instead of being dropped.

label_rule: Gold is the capability that should serve the request, read against app/agent/intents.yaml, not against the classifier's cue table. A request to move money is REFUND_REQUEST even when it names an order; a request to register a case is TICKET_CREATE even when the cause is a delivery problem; a question about a rule is POLICY_QA even when no policy document covers the topic, because the no-evidence path is the expected behaviour. When a sentence could be about order fields or transport position, ORDER_QUERY covers fields (payment, address, amount) and LOGISTICS_QUERY covers where the parcel is. REFUND_ELIGIBILITY asks whether this order or return qualifies and usually names the user's own item or action; POLICY_QA asks what the rule says in general. UNKNOWN means no catalog capability should serve it, not 'the classifier is unsure'.
